implementation_notes: Ruby's core library provides thread-safe handoff (Thread::Queue) and timing (Thread::ConditionVariable, whose wait accepts a timeout), but the pending window itself is a Hash keyed by sequence number guarded by a Mutex, with delete-if-expected as the cursor. concurrent-ruby's Concurrent::PriorityQueue is the closest ready-made ordered structure and its documentation notes that it performs no blocking and is not thread safe on its own, so the surrounding Mutex remains. In Ruby the resequencer is nearly always written by hand inside a consumer or a background job; no framework ships an equivalent of Camel's resequence step.
pitfalls: Hash#delete on the expected key makes the cursor loop O(1), but an unbounded Hash is a memory leak: bound the window and expire holes explicitly.

Thread::Queue#pop blocks and ConditionVariable#wait must be called with the mutex held, so mixing them without one lock discipline deadlocks; keep the window update and the release decision in the same critical section.
Fibers and Ractors do not share ordinary mutable state, so a Hash/Mutex resequencer must stay inside one Ractor; cross-Ractor handoff needs a Channel instead.
